home.title: Yulting Rinpoche
home.subtitle: Educator, translator, and Buddhist scholar
home.bio: Based at Gaden Shartse Monastery, I am dedicated to sharing Buddhist teachings and exploring where contemplative practice meets modern understanding. This site is a place to share reflections, translations, and resources with fellow seekers.
home.welcomeText: This site is a modest offering — a place to gather teachings, translations, and reflections in one accessible space. Whether you are a student of Buddhism, a fellow scholar, or simply curious, you are welcome here.
home.offeringTeachingsDesc: Reflections on Buddhist philosophy drawn from study and practice at Gaden Shartse.
home.offeringTranslationsDesc: Work in English-Tibetan translation, bridging monastic scholarship and wider audiences.
home.offeringReflectionsDesc: Thoughts on education, contemplative life, and the meeting of tradition and modernity.
home.ctaText: Whether you have a question, a thought to share, or simply wish to connect, I would be glad to hear from you.

about.metaDescription: Learn about Yulting Rinpoche — educator, translator, and Buddhist scholar at Gaden Shartse Monastery.
about.bio1: I am a Tibetan Buddhist monk based at Gaden Shartse Monastery in southern India. Born in Nepal in 1994, I was recognized as a reincarnated Tulku and have spent most of my life in monastic study — learning from my teachers, debating with fellow students, and trying to deepen my understanding of the Dharma.
about.bio2: This website is a small effort to share some of what I have been learning, in the hope that it may be of benefit to others.
about.studiesText1: I have been studying the traditional Gelug curriculum at Gaden Shartse Monastery, covering the major texts on logic, the Perfection of Wisdom, the Middle Way, metaphysics, and monastic ethics. I am currently preparing for the Geshe Lharampa examination, which is the final stage of this course of study.
about.studiesText2: Alongside the classical curriculum, I completed six years of the monastery's Comprehensive Science Program, which introduced subjects like physics, biology, and neuroscience alongside Buddhist philosophy. This experience opened my eyes to the many points of contact between contemplative traditions and modern science.
about.teachingText1: For the past several years, I have been teaching English-Tibetan translation at Gaden Shartse School, helping fellow monks develop the language skills needed to engage with a wider world. Before that, I had the opportunity to offer teachings in Buddhist philosophy and practice to students at the monastery.
about.teachingText2: Translation work has become a meaningful part of my life — I have served as a translator for the Emory Tibet Science Initiative and at various seminars and workshops where monastic scholars and scientists come together. I find this work deeply rewarding, as it helps bridge two rich traditions of inquiry.
about.engagementsText1: I have had the good fortune to participate in gatherings beyond the monastery, including the Second Indo-Tibetan Scholars Conference, where I spoke about contemplative practice and Buddhist psychology. I have also given Dharma talks in Singapore and other places when invited.
about.engagementsText2: These experiences have taught me a great deal about how the Dharma can speak to people in different contexts and cultures. I remain a student above all, grateful for every opportunity to learn and share.

translations.subtitle: Bridging Tibetan and English.
translations.metaDescription: English–Tibetan translation work by Yulting Rinpoche, bridging monastic scholarship and wider audiences.
translations.intro1: Translation is a central part of my work — carrying texts and teachings between Tibetan and English, so that monastic scholarship can reach wider audiences and students of the Dharma can meet the tradition in their own language.
translations.intro2: This page will grow as translation projects are completed and published. In the meantime, translated teachings appear throughout the writings and teachings on this site.
translations.cta: If you would like to discuss a translation project, please get in touch.
